title: Pinakbet (Filipino Vegetable Stew with Prawns and Shrimp Paste)
summary: Garlic, tomato paste and shrimp paste fried to a deep savoury base, then simmered with tomato, onion and squash before the green vegetables and bitter melon go in. Prawns are cooked through at the end. No extra salt is needed.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven with lid

ingredients.note: the pink, untoasted kind; it is the only salt in the dish

ingredients.item: kabocha squash, peeled and cut into 4 cm pieces
long beans or green beans, cut into 5 cm lengths
long aubergine, cut into 2.5 cm pieces
bitter melon, halved, seeded and cut into 1 cm half-moons
portions steamed jasmine rice, to serve

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Heat the oil in the pot over medium-high heat and cook the garlic for 2-3 min until soft. Stir in the tomato paste for 2 min until it turns brick red, then add the bagoong and fry for 1-2 min until it smells strong and toasty.

steps.title: Simmer the squash
steps.text: Add the tomatoes and stir for 2-3 min, scraping up the sticky base, then add the onion, squash and 360 ml water. Simmer briskly for 10 min, stirring now and then, until the squash begins to soften and the sauce looks glossy.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the okra, beans, aubergine and bitter melon and stir to coat. Cook for 5 min, then turn the heat to medium-low and cook for 12-15 min more, stirring gently so the squash does not break up, until everything is tender.

steps.title: Cook the prawns
steps.text: Tuck the prawns into the vegetables, cover and cook for 3-4 min until pink and opaque right through (63 °C). Serve hot with steamed rice.

tips: Bagoong varies a lot in saltiness; start with 1.5 tbsp and taste before adding the rest.
Salting the sliced bitter melon for 10 min, then rinsing it, tames its bitterness.
Leftover roast chicken or fried tofu can replace the prawns.
storage: Refrigerate up to 2 days. Reheat until piping hot (74 °C); the prawns will firm up a little. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
